q1_issues.issue: The definite anaphoric subject "The mist-light" is filled by the bare kind symbol mist_light, which the parse also puts in class position (mist_light_genus), whereas a specific definite referent must be a typed witness.
"Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron" fills Patient with the bare kind mire_essence instead of a witness for the specific portion that formed.
The definite "the mire-essence" reuses that same kind symbol, so the stored portion is not distinguished from the mire-essence the lantern burned in sentence 2.
"the stored mire-essence" both reuses the bare kind symbol and silently drops the participial modifier "stored", which as a modifier is an adjective and licenses its own atom.
"left silken threads" takes Patient although leaving/depositing neither creates, destroys, consumes nor changes the threads, so the role test (and its unclear-case default) gives Theme.

Sentence 7's "at the Harbor Row" surfaces only as (LocatedIn sk_crowd_1 harbor_row), leaving the hunting event with no locative, though the event-modifier attachment is at least as available there as the NP-modifier one.

q2_gaps: A fictional-calendar date "day 380 of Year 2" — a day-of-year number with no month, inside a bare ordinal year: the Time section's (Day n)/(Year n) terms assume a Gregorian day-of-month and calendar year, and nothing states how such a date should be rendered.

An ordinal-modified noun with no associated ordering event and no explicit "-est" dimension ("the second cauldron") — Ordinal's scale slot is specified only as the associated event or a stated dimension, so no licensed filler exists.
notes: Event structure, compound decomposition, group/cardinality handling, the per-member distribution rules and the time atoms are otherwise accurate, and every head used is licensed. The systematic defect is that mass referents (mist-light, mire-essence) stay bare kind symbols even when definite, so one symbol occupies both class and individual positions and merges distinct portions across the passage.
